sections.title: The two ways
The king the LORD has anointed
A shield all around me
Lying down in peace
A prayer at daybreak
A prayer from a bed of tears
A plea to the righteous judge
Your name across the whole earth
Thanks to the judge of the world
Why do you keep so far away?
Refuge when the foundations give way
Pure words in a time of lies
How long, LORD?
No one who does good
Who may stay in God’s tent?
My share is the LORD
Hide me in the shadow of your wings
David’s song of rescue and victory
Heavens and instruction tell God’s glory
A prayer for the king before battle
The king rejoices in the LORD’s strength
From forsaken to praise among the nations
The LORD, my shepherd and host
The King of glory comes in
Teach me your paths and forgive me
Judge me, for I walk with integrity
The LORD is my light
My rock, do not be silent
The voice of the LORD in the storm
Mourning turned into dancing
Into your hand I commit my spirit
The joy of sin forgiven
Praise the Creator who rules the nations
Taste and see the LORD’s goodness
Fight for me, LORD
Rebellion’s whisper and God’s wide love
Do not fret; wait for the LORD
Prayer of a sick and guilty sufferer
My life is only a breath
A new song, then a cry for help
Betrayed by a friend, upheld by God
Thirsty for the living God
Send out your light and truth
Faithful, yet crushed: wake up, Lord
A wedding song for the king
God is with us in the shaking world
God goes up as King of all the earth
Zion, the city of the great King
No one can buy a way out of death
God brings his people to court
Create a pure heart in me
The boaster and the olive tree
Not one does good
God, save me by your name
Betrayed by a close friend
When I am afraid, I trust
Shelter in the shadow of your wings
A God who judges the earth
Rescue from enemies who prowl at night
Help against the foe after defeat
Lead me to the rock higher than I
Wait quietly for God alone
Thirsting for God in a dry land
God’s arrows against secret plotters
Praise for the God who sends rain
Come and see what God has done
May all the peoples praise you, God
God marches from Sinai to Zion
Rescue me from the deep waters
Hurry, God, and help me
Do not leave me now I am old
A prayer for the king’s reign
Envy of the wicked, and nearness to God
Remember your people and your ruined sanctuary
God is judge: he lowers and lifts
God breaks the weapons at Zion
Remembering God’s way through the sea
Tell the next generation: grace despite rebellion
A plea for ruined Jerusalem
Restore your vine, God of Armies
If only my people would listen
God judges the gods
Do not keep silent, God
Longing for the LORD’s house
Loyal love and faithfulness meet
Unite my heart to fear your name
The nations born in Zion
A prayer from the darkness
Your promise to David, and the fallen crown
Teach us to count our days
In the shelter of the Most High
It is good to give thanks
The LORD is King
God who judges the earth, rise up
Bow to the King; listen today
A new song for all the earth
The LORD is King over all
Creation greets its coming Judge
Holy is the King enthroned in Zion
All the earth, come in with thanks
A king’s vow of integrity
A prayer from the ashes for Zion
Bless the LORD, my soul
The Creator’s world, full of creatures
The LORD keeps his promise
Israel’s unfaithfulness and God’s mercy
Let the rescued give thanks
Morning praise and a prayer for victory
God of my praise, do not be silent
A king and priest forever
The great works of the LORD
The life of one who fears the LORD
The LORD lifts up the lowly
When Israel came out of Egypt
Not to us, but to your name
I love the LORD, who heard me
All nations, praise the LORD
The stone the builders cast aside
Your word, my delight and my life
Living among people who hate peace
The LORD guards your going and coming
Pray for Jerusalem’s peace
Eyes on the LORD, like a servant’s on a master
If the LORD had not been on our side
Like Mount Zion, which cannot be shaken
Bring us back like streams in the Negev
Unless the LORD builds the house
The blessing on those who fear the LORD
Attacked often, never defeated
Out of the depths, waiting for the Lord
Calm like a weaned child
The LORD’s oath to David and his choice of Zion
How good it is to live as one
Bless the LORD by night
Praise the LORD, who chose Israel
His loyal love lasts forever
By the rivers of Babylon
Thanks for an answered prayer
The LORD knows me through and through
Rescue me from violent people
A guard over my mouth
A prayer from the cave
Do not bring your servant to trial
A prayer for the king’s victory
My God the King, forever praised
Trust the God of Jacob, not rulers
The LORD who counts stars and heals
All creation, praise the LORD
A new song for the faithful
Everything that breathes, praise him

summaries.1: The one who delights in God’s instruction is like a tree planted by streams of water, while the wicked are like chaff that the wind blows away.
summaries.2: The nations plot against God and the anointed king, but God laughs at them and declares the king to be God’s son, set on Zion; the rulers are warned to serve God.
summaries.3: David, fleeing from Absalom, cries out that his enemies are many, yet he lies down and sleeps, for God is his shield and rescue.
summaries.4: David calls on God to answer him and tells others to trust God; God has given him more joy than a rich harvest, and he sleeps in peace.
summaries.5: David prays in the morning for God to hear him and lead him in righteousness, for God hates evil, and he asks God to protect those who take refuge in God.
summaries.6: In distress and illness David begs God not to correct him in anger; worn out with weeping, he is sure that God has heard his cry.
summaries.7: David takes refuge in God against those who pursue him and asks God, the righteous judge, to vindicate him.
summaries.8: God’s name is glorious in all the earth; when David looks at the heavens he wonders that God cares for human beings and has crowned them with glory over all creation.
summaries.9: David thanks God for judging the nations with justice and for being a stronghold for the oppressed, who are not forgotten.
summaries.10: The psalmist asks why God seems far away while the wicked hunt down the poor, and calls on God to rise up, for God hears the afflicted and defends the fatherless.
summaries.11: When advised to flee like a bird, David declares that he takes refuge in God, who sees from heaven and loves justice.
summaries.12: When the faithful have vanished and everyone speaks lies, God promises to rise up for the poor, and God’s words are pure as refined silver.
summaries.13: David asks how long God will forget him, then trusts in God’s loyal love and sings of God’s goodness.
summaries.14: Fools say there is no God, and no one does good, yet God is with the righteous and will restore the fortunes of God’s people.
summaries.15: David asks who may dwell on God’s holy mountain: the one who walks without blame, speaks truth and keeps his word.
summaries.16: David has made God his refuge and his portion; he will not be abandoned to the grave but shown the path of life and fullness of joy.
summaries.17: David appeals to God to hear his just cause and to hide him in the shadow of God’s wings from the wicked.
summaries.18: David sings of the day God rescued him from all his enemies: God, his rock and fortress, came down in storm and thunder and drew him out of deep waters.
summaries.19: The heavens declare God’s glory, and God’s instruction is perfect, more precious than gold; David prays that his words and thoughts may please God.
summaries.20: The people pray that God will answer the king in the day of trouble and give him victory, for they trust not in chariots but in God’s name.
summaries.21: The king rejoices in God’s strength and saving help, and trusts that God will defeat his enemies.
summaries.22: David cries, "My God, my God, why have you abandoned me?" surrounded by mocking enemies, then praises God who has heard him, and all the earth will turn to God.
summaries.23: God is David’s shepherd, who leads him to rest, guides him through the darkest valley and spreads a table before him; goodness and love will follow him all his life.
summaries.24: The earth belongs to God, who made it; those with clean hands may stand in God’s holy place, and the gates are told to open for the King of glory.
summaries.25: David lifts up his whole self to God, asks to be taught God’s ways and forgiven, and trusts God to rescue him.
summaries.26: David asks God to examine him, for he has walked with integrity and loves the house where God’s glory dwells.
summaries.27: God is David’s light and salvation, so he has no one to fear; he asks to live in God’s house and urges waiting for God.
summaries.28: David cries out to God, his rock, to hear him and not count him with the wicked, and praises God who has heard.
summaries.29: The heavenly beings are called to give God glory, whose voice thunders over the waters and shakes the wilderness, and who blesses the people with peace.
summaries.30: David praises God for lifting him up from the grave; weeping may last for the night, but joy comes in the morning.
summaries.31: David commits his spirit into God’s hand, tells of his distress and the plots against him, and praises God’s goodness to those who take refuge in God.
summaries.32: Those whose rebellion is forgiven are blessed; when David kept silent he wasted away, but when he confessed, God forgave him.
summaries.33: The righteous are called to sing a new song to God, whose word made the heavens and whose eye is on those who fear God and hope in God’s loyal love.
summaries.34: David praises God, who answered him and delivered him from all his fears, and invites others to taste and see that God is good.
summaries.35: David asks God to fight those who fight against him and repay those who return evil for good.
summaries.36: The wicked have no fear of God, but God’s loyal love reaches to the heavens, and with God is the fountain of life.
summaries.37: The righteous are told not to fret over evildoers, who will soon wither, but to trust God and wait patiently, for the meek will inherit the land.
summaries.38: Sick and burdened by guilt, abandoned by friends, David confesses his sin and pleads with God not to forsake him.
summaries.39: David reflects that human life is a breath and asks God to show him how short his days are; his hope is in God.
summaries.40: David waited patiently for God, who drew him up from the pit and put a new song in his mouth; he delights to do God’s will.
summaries.41: Those who care for the weak are blessed; in sickness, betrayed even by a close friend, David asks God to raise him up.
summaries.42: Like a deer longing for streams, the psalmist thirsts for God, and asks his soul why it is downcast: hope in God.
summaries.43: The psalmist asks God to send out light and truth to lead him to God’s altar, and again urges his soul to hope in God.
summaries.44: Israel recalls God’s deeds for their ancestors, yet now they are defeated and scorned though they have not forgotten God; they cry out for God to wake and help.
summaries.45: A love song for the king’s wedding praises the king’s majesty and righteous rule and calls the bride to honor him.
summaries.46: God is our refuge and strength, so we will not fear though the earth gives way; God is in the city, and the nations are told to be still and know God.
summaries.47: All peoples are called to clap and shout to God, the great King over all the earth.
summaries.48: Zion, the city of God, is beautiful and secure; kings who saw it fled in terror, and God will guide God’s people forever.
summaries.49: Wealth cannot ransom anyone from death; the rich and the foolish perish alike, but God will redeem the psalmist’s life from the grave.
summaries.50: God summons heaven and earth to judge the people: God needs no sacrifices but wants thanksgiving and faithfulness, and rebukes the wicked.
summaries.51: After Nathan confronts him about Bathsheba, David pleads for mercy and cleansing, asking God to create in him a clean heart; God does not despise a broken spirit.
summaries.52: David denounces the boastful man who trusts in wealth and lies, while he is like an olive tree flourishing in God’s house.
summaries.53: Fools say there is no God, and no one does good, yet God will scatter the enemies and restore God’s people.
summaries.54: When the Ziphites betray him, David asks God to save him and vindicate him, and promises to offer thanks.
summaries.55: David grieves that a close friend has betrayed him; he longs for wings to fly away, but casts his burden on God.
summaries.56: When the Philistines seize him in Gath, David trusts God and is not afraid, for God keeps count of his tears.
summaries.57: Hiding in the cave from Saul, David takes refuge in the shadow of God’s wings and resolves to sing God’s praise among the nations.
summaries.58: David denounces unjust rulers and asks God to break their power, so that people will know that God judges the earth.
summaries.59: When Saul’s men watch his house, David asks God to rescue him from his enemies and praises God as his fortress.
summaries.60: After defeat, the people ask God to restore them, and God promises to divide the land and humble their enemies.
summaries.61: From the ends of the earth David cries out to God, his rock and refuge, and prays for the king’s long life.
summaries.62: David waits in quiet for God alone, his rock and salvation, and urges people to trust in God at all times rather than in wealth.
summaries.63: In the wilderness David thirsts for God, whose loyal love is better than life, and clings to God.
summaries.64: David asks God to protect him from the secret plots of evildoers, whom God will strike down.
summaries.65: God answers prayer, forgives, and crowns the year with abundance, making the meadows and valleys shout for joy.
summaries.66: All the earth is called to praise God for awesome deeds, such as bringing Israel through the sea and through trials, and the psalmist tells what God has done for him.
summaries.67: The people pray that God will bless them so that all nations will know God’s ways and praise God.
summaries.68: God rises up and enemies scatter; God, father of the fatherless, leads the people from Sinai to the sanctuary, and the kingdoms of the earth are called to sing to God.
summaries.69: Sinking in deep water and hated without cause, the psalmist pleads for rescue and asks God to repay his enemies.
summaries.70: David asks God to hurry to save him, and to let all who seek God rejoice.
summaries.71: From his youth to old age the psalmist has relied on God, and he asks God not to forsake him now that he is gray.
summaries.72: A prayer for the king asks that he judge the poor with justice, rule from sea to sea, and that all nations be blessed through him.
summaries.73: Asaph nearly stumbled when he saw the wicked prosper, until he entered God’s sanctuary and understood their end; God is his portion forever.
summaries.74: The psalmist mourns the enemies’ destruction of the sanctuary and asks God to remember the covenant and rise up.
summaries.75: The people give thanks to God, who judges in due time, humbling some and lifting up others.
summaries.76: God is renowned in Judah and breaks the weapons of war; God judges to save the humble of the earth.
summaries.77: In distress the psalmist wonders whether God has forgotten to be gracious, then remembers God’s wonders of old, when God led the people through the sea.
summaries.78: Asaph tells the next generation of God’s wonders in Egypt and the wilderness and of Israel’s repeated rebellion, and how God chose Judah, Zion and David to shepherd the people.
summaries.79: The nations have defiled the temple and laid Jerusalem in ruins, and the people ask God to forgive and to avenge them.
summaries.80: The people pray to the Shepherd of Israel to restore them, picturing Israel as a vine brought out of Egypt and now cut down, and ask God to turn the light of God’s face on them so they will be saved.
summaries.81: The people are called to celebrate a festival, and God speaks, longing for Israel to listen and walk in God’s ways.
summaries.82: God judges among the gods, rebuking them for failing to defend the weak and the fatherless, and the psalmist calls on God to judge the earth.
summaries.83: Enemy nations conspire against Israel, and the psalmist asks God to deal with them as with enemies of old, so that they may know God alone is Most High.
summaries.84: The psalmist longs for God’s dwelling place; one day in God’s courts is better than a thousand elsewhere.
summaries.85: The people recall how God forgave and restored them and ask God to do so again; loyal love and faithfulness meet as friends, and righteousness and peace greet each other with a kiss.
summaries.86: David, afflicted and in need, asks God to answer him and to teach him God’s way, for God is merciful and gracious.
summaries.87: God loves Zion, and people of many nations will be counted as born there.
summaries.88: Heman cries out from the edge of death, abandoned by friends, with darkness as his only companion.
summaries.89: Ethan sings of God’s loyal love and the covenant with David, then laments that God seems to have rejected the anointed king, and asks how long.
summaries.90: Moses prays to God, who has been the people’s home in every generation, and asks God to teach them to reckon their days rightly and establish the work of their hands.
summaries.91: Whoever lives under the shelter of the Most High will be protected from every danger, for God promises to rescue the one who loves God.
summaries.92: It is good to give thanks to God, whose works are great; the righteous flourish like palm trees.
summaries.93: God is King, robed in majesty, mightier than the roaring waters, and God’s decrees stand firm.
summaries.94: The psalmist calls on God, the Judge of all the earth, to repay the arrogant, and finds comfort in God’s support when his foot slips.
summaries.95: The people are called to sing to God, the great King, and to worship, but warned not to harden their hearts as their ancestors did in the wilderness.
summaries.96: All the earth is called to sing a new song to God, who is to be feared above all gods and comes to judge the world in righteousness.
summaries.97: God is King; fire and lightning go before God, idols are put to shame, and the righteous rejoice.
summaries.98: All the earth is called to sing a new song to God for the wonders God has done and the victory God has won, for God comes to judge.
summaries.99: God is King, enthroned on the cherubim, holy and just, who answered Moses, Aaron and Samuel.
summaries.100: All the earth is called to shout for joy to God, who made us and whose loyal love lasts forever.
summaries.101: David resolves to live with integrity and to have nothing to do with the wicked.
summaries.102: A person in deep trouble pours out a complaint to God, whose years never end, and trusts that God will rebuild Zion.
summaries.103: The psalmist calls on himself to bless God, who forgives, heals and redeems, and whose loyal love is as high as the heavens.
summaries.104: The psalmist blesses God for creation, the heavens, the waters, the creatures and the seasons, all of which look to God for life.
summaries.105: The people are called to give thanks for God’s covenant with Abraham and the wonders God did through Joseph, Moses and the exodus.
summaries.106: Israel confesses its repeated sins from Egypt to the land, and God’s repeated mercy, and asks God to gather them from the nations.
summaries.107: Those whom God has redeemed are called to give thanks: wanderers, prisoners, the sick and sailors in a storm all cried out, and God rescued them.
summaries.108: David’s heart is firm, and he praises God among the nations and trusts God for victory.
summaries.109: Attacked by liars, David asks God to deal with his accuser and to save him because of God’s loyal love.
summaries.110: God declares to the king, "Take your seat at my right hand," and makes him a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.
summaries.111: The psalmist praises God’s great works, faithful covenant and redemption; the fear of God is where wisdom begins.
summaries.112: Those who fear God and delight in God’s commands are blessed; they are generous and need not fear bad news.
summaries.113: The servants of God are called to praise the name of God, who is enthroned on high and lifts up the poor.
summaries.114: When Israel left Egypt, the sea fled and the mountains skipped before God.
summaries.115: Glory belongs to God’s name, not to us; idols are lifeless, but God blesses those who trust in God.
summaries.116: The psalmist loves God, who heard his cry when death surrounded him, and he will keep his vows.
summaries.117: All nations are called to praise God, whose loyal love is great.
summaries.118: The people give thanks to God, whose loyal love lasts forever; the stone the builders cast aside is now the stone at the head of the corner.
summaries.119: In twenty-two sections, one for each letter of the alphabet, the psalmist delights in God’s instruction, prays to keep it, and finds it a lamp for his feet.
summaries.120: In trouble among liars and people who hate peace, the psalmist cries out to God.
summaries.121: The psalmist’s help comes from God, who made heaven and earth and who will guard his going out and coming in.
summaries.122: Pilgrims rejoice to stand in Jerusalem and pray for its peace.
summaries.123: As servants watch their master’s hand, the people look to God for mercy.
summaries.124: If God had not been on Israel’s side, they would have been swept away; their help is in God’s name.
summaries.125: Those who trust God are like Mount Zion, which cannot be shaken.
summaries.126: When God restored Zion’s fortunes the people laughed for joy, and they pray that those who sow in tears will reap with songs of joy.
summaries.127: Unless God builds the house, its builders work in vain; children are a gift from God.
summaries.128: Those who fear God are blessed with fruitful work and family.
summaries.129: Israel’s enemies have attacked since its youth but have not prevailed, and the psalmist prays that they will be put to shame.
summaries.130: From the depths the psalmist cries to God, who forgives, and he waits for God more than watchmen wait for morning.
summaries.131: The psalmist has calmed and quieted himself like a weaned child, and urges Israel to hope in God.
summaries.132: The people ask God to remember David, and God swears to keep David’s line on the throne and to dwell in Zion.
summaries.133: How good it is when God’s people live together in unity.
summaries.134: The servants of God in the house of God are called to bless God at night.
summaries.135: The people praise God, who chose Jacob, does whatever God pleases and brought Israel out of Egypt; idols are lifeless.
summaries.136: Each line of thanks to God for creation and for rescuing Israel answers that God’s loyal love lasts forever.
summaries.137: By the rivers of Babylon the exiles weep as they remember Zion and cannot sing God’s song in a foreign land.
summaries.138: David gives thanks for God’s loyal love and faithfulness, for God looks on the lowly and will fulfill God’s purpose for him.
summaries.139: God knows the psalmist completely, is present everywhere and formed him in the womb; he asks God to search him and lead him.
summaries.140: David asks God to rescue him from violent and slanderous people.
summaries.141: David asks God to keep watch over his mouth and to keep him from the snares of the wicked.
summaries.142: In the cave David cries out to God, for no one cares for him, and God is his refuge.
summaries.143: David pleads for mercy, for no one living is righteous before God, and asks God to teach him to do God’s will.
summaries.144: David blesses God, his rock, who trains him for battle, and prays for a blessed and prosperous people.
summaries.145: David praises God, the King, who is gracious and merciful, near to all who call, and whose kingdom lasts forever.
summaries.146: The psalmist will praise God all his life, for God, not princes, made heaven and earth and gives justice to the oppressed.
summaries.147: God rebuilds Jerusalem, heals the brokenhearted, counts the stars and sends the snow, and delights in those who fear God.
summaries.148: The heavens, the earth and all creatures are called to praise God.
summaries.149: The faithful are called to sing a new song and to praise God with dancing, for God delights in the people.
summaries.150: Everything that has breath is called to praise God with trumpet, harp, strings and cymbals.
